mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on a joint state where one team (Team B) holds structurally high possession (all-prior mean ~61%) while the opponent (Team A) is near 50/50, then jointly examine each team's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio. This requires simultaneously conditioning on possession imbalance AND the joint shot/on-target relationship for both sides — not reducible to a single observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The high-possession team's shots-on-target as a share of total shots is suppressed relative to the lower-possession team's equivalent ratio when possession imbalance is large; i.e., volume of shots rises with possession dominance but on-target conversion rate does not rise proportionally.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a large possession imbalance exists between two teams (Team B structurally dominates possession while Team A is near-parity), the relationship between each team's shots and shots-on-target diverges asymmetrically: the high-possession team's shot volume does not proportionally translate into on-target accuracy, while the lower-possession team's on-target rate relative to total shots may be comparatively higher.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint three-variable relationship (possession, shots, shots_on_target) across two sides simultaneously, with an asymmetric cross-team comparison. It cannot be reduced to any single observable mirror, a single observable with one band, or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession level and corner production. Team B holds ~61% possession all-prior but generates ~5.2 corners (near competition mean of ~5.0), while Team A holds ~49% possession but also generates ~4.9 corners. Measure whether, across historical matches, teams with possession levels as high as Team B's generate corners at a rate proportionally above competition baseline, or whether the relationship saturates.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner production saturates or decouples from possession share beyond a threshold level of possession dominance; teams with very high possession do not generate proportionally more corners than near-parity teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's structurally high possession does not translate into a proportionally high corner-kick yield, while Team A generates corners near the competition average despite lower possession. The joint relationship between possession dominance and corner production differs across the two teams, suggesting that corner generation is not simply a function of possession share.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a threshold/saturation non-linear relationship between a continuous possession variable and corner output — not a simple single-observable mirror or coarse band split. It requires jointly examining two observables across both teams against a competition baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on each team's foul-committed rate and second-half card rate, comparing the cross-team asymmetry: Team A commits fewer fouls (10.0) than it receives (12.6), while Team B commits more fouls (11.8) than it receives (13.6 against). Measure whether the team that commits more fouls in a matchup accumulates more second-half cards, and whether the direction of the foul imbalance predicts which side's cards_2h is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with the higher foul-commit rate relative to its opponent's foul-commit rate accumulates more second-half cards; the cross-team foul asymmetry rises with second-half card asymmetry.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The relationship between a team's foul rate and its second-half card accumulation is asymmetric across the two sides: Team A concedes more fouls against it (opponent fouls on Team A) than it commits, while Team B concedes more fouls against it than it commits in recent matches. The joint cross-team pattern of who commits fouls versus who receives second-half cards differs structurally, and this asymmetry is measurable as a joint two-observable, two-team relationship.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (fouls, cards_2h), two-team asymmetric relationship. It requires simultaneously conditioning on both teams' foul rates and comparing the directional cross-team imbalance against second-half card outcomes — not reducible to a single observable mirror or one-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state of a team's recent-window foul rate versus all-prior foul rate, and simultaneously examine whether the cards_2h rate diverges from what the full-match yellow card rate implies. For Team B, recent fouls (9.8) are notably below all-prior (11.8), while cards_2h against Team B (1.8) remains elevated. Measure whether the gap between recent and all-prior foul rates predicts a divergence between full-match yellow cards and second-half card concentration.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent foul rate drops below its all-prior rate, second-half card concentration (cards_2h relative to yellow_cards) rises rather than falls, suggesting disciplinary pressure accumulates in the second half independently of first-half foul volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The relationship between a team's full-match foul rate and its yellow card accumulation differs between first and second halves. Specifically, when a team's recent foul rate diverges from its all-prior foul rate, the second-half card rate (cards_2h) may be disproportionately affected relative to what the full-match yellow card rate would suggest, indicating a within-match state-dependent accumulation pattern.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three observables jointly (fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) with a within-match half-level split and a recent-vs-all-prior regime comparison simultaneously — structurally richer than any single-observable recent-vs-long-run comparison or a single half-level split alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession level and offside rate (both all-prior and recent), then examine second-half goal rates. Team A: recent offsides FOR dropped to 1.0 (from 1.8 all-prior) while possession rose to 57.2% (from 49.3%); Team B: offsides FOR at 2.1 all-prior, rising to 3.0 recent, with possession at ~61%. Measure whether the combination of high possession AND high offsides (aggressive line-breaking) is associated with elevated second-half goals, versus high possession with low offsides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal production rises when a team jointly exhibits high possession and high offside rate (indicating aggressive forward runs against a high defensive line), compared to teams with high possession but low offside rates; the joint possession-offside interaction predicts second-half goal rate above what either variable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between a team's possession level, its offside rate, and its second-half goal production captures a structural attacking pattern: teams that hold high possession and generate high offsides (indicating high defensive lines and aggressive forward runs) may show a different second-half goal rate than teams with similar possession but lower offsides. Team A's recent offside rate has dropped sharply while possession has risen, and Team B maintains elevated offsides with high possession — this joint pattern across both teams relates to second-half goal production.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint three-variable relationship (possession, offsides, goals) with a within-match half-level split, combining a recent-vs-all-prior regime shift in one variable (offsides) with a simultaneous possession level — not reducible to any single-observable comparison or one-band conditioning.
